title: Lesson 39: Transaction Lifecycle: State, Save Order, and the 4 Trigger Contexts in One Transaction
description: The fixed sequence a record save walks from load to commit, what lives in the database versus in memory at each phase, and the four trigger contexts one transaction can run.

questions.question: Where should a trigger set or normalize a field on the record being saved, and why?
options: In before context, where the change persists with no extra DML.
In after context, because the record already has an Id at that point.
In a separate DML update issued after the trigger finishes running.
In a validation rule, which modifies field values before the record writes.
questions.explanation: Values set on the in-memory record in before context are persisted by the same save with no separate DML statement, which keeps the transaction small.

questions.question: An after-update trigger reads a parent's roll-up summary field to make a decision. What is wrong?
options: Nothing; roll-up summaries are recalculated before after triggers run.
Roll-ups recalculate after after triggers, so the value is stale.
Roll-up summary fields cannot be read from Apex trigger code at all.
The trigger should read Trigger.old instead of the parent roll-up.
questions.explanation: Roll-up recalculation happens near the end of the save, well after after triggers, so an after trigger reading the roll-up sees the pre-recalculation value.

questions.question: A batch upserts 5,000 records, some new and some existing, in one transaction. Which save contexts run?
options: Only before insert and after insert, because upsert is treated as an insert.
Only before update and after update, because existing records dominate the set.
All four contexts, so the trigger must dispatch on the operation it faces.
No contexts run, because batch operations bypass record triggers.
questions.explanation: A transaction is not limited to one operation, so a mixed upsert runs before insert, before update, after insert, and after update, and the trigger must dispatch on the operation rather than assume one.
